Creative.tagline: AI tools for the writers who annotate.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Marginalia is the real Latin-rooted word for notes written in the margins of a book — deeply literary, archaic, immediately readable to anyone who reads carefully. AI is the plain category suffix. Stands in the lineage of literary-rooted modern tool naming (Notion, Linear).
Creative.manifesto: Most AI brands sell the magic. The glowing figure. The future of work. We made Marginalia AI because the actual experience of working with AI is mostly debugging. Re-writing the prompt. Re-running the output. Squinting at the result. Marginalia AI is the brand for the real experience: a tool that helps you write better prompts, with humor and humility about how often we all type the wrong thing.
Creative.industrySummary: AI tool branding has been polished, futuristic, and slightly cold. There's room for one that's loud, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and honest about how AI actually works in daily use.
Creative.competitorLandscape: ChatGPT (chat.openai.com) is the cultural reference. Cursor (cursor.com) holds the developer-tool peer. Cleo (meetcleo.com) does playful in fintech-AI. Krea (krea.ai) does design-led AI image work. We sit warmer than all of them, with a clearer point of view.
Creative.positioningStatement: An AI tool that helps you write better prompts and laughs about the bad ones.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Already uses three AI tools. Has typed at least one prompt today they regret. Wants a tool that's good at output and good at admitting when the output is wrong.

dos: Show the bad output and the better one
Talk to the user like another tired AI user

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a foundation-model lab. Not an enterprise AI consultancy. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to admit a prompt was bad.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: A product that shows the bad output and the better prompt side by side. Stickers in every welcome email (digital and physical). A weekly newsletter with the funniest bad prompts from the community. A merch line for the patient few: tees that say Marginalia AI across the back.

Creative.brandDescription: An AI tool that helps you write better prompts and laughs about the bad ones.
Creative.mission: To build an AI tool that helps you write better prompts and laughs about the bad ones.
Creative.vision: Marginalia AI is the brand for the real experience: a tool that helps you write better prompts, with humor and humility about how often we all type the wrong thing.
coreValues: Playful — seriousness is overrated.
Sharp — precision is a form of kindness.
Warm — we are friendly, not formal.
Direct — we say what we mean without softening it.
Confident — we stand behind the work, not the marketing.
Creative.scope:
Marginalia AI delivers by:
• Quote real bad prompts (with humor)
• Show the bad output and the better one
• Talk to the user like another tired AI user

Creative.tagline: An AI tools company for the people who write the prompts.
Creative.brandDescription: The Prompt Office is a creative-led AI tools company building prompt-engineering workspaces, evaluation tooling, and version control for teams that write prompts as a primary deliverable.
Creative.scope:
The Prompt Office works across:
• Collaborative prompt-engineering workspaces
• Prompt evaluation and regression testing
• Version control and audit trails for prompts in production
• Educational resources for prompt-engineering as a discipline
• Quarterly essays on the craft of prompt engineering
Creative.mission: To treat prompt engineering as the discipline it has become.
Creative.vision: A workspace where every team writing prompts in production tracks them with the same rigor engineers track code.
coreValues: Specific — every prompt is tracked.
Considered — prompt engineering is a discipline.
Warm — the workspace respects the writer.
Literary — the writing about the craft is part of the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Prompt Office is a declarative naming convention — naming the company after the workspace where prompts are written — borrowed from OMA's full original name (Office for Metropolitan Architecture). The definite article + trade-noun + Office format reads as a small declarative outfit with a clear creative position. Stands in the lineage of creative-led AI tooling brands (Anthropic's Console register, Perplexity's interface tradition).
Creative.manifesto: Most AI tools companies treat prompts as configuration. We started The Prompt Office because prompts have become a serious deliverable — written, versioned, tested, deployed — and the people writing them deserve tools that respect that work. The workspace is for the prompt engineer.
Creative.industrySummary: Prompt engineering has emerged as a recognized discipline but most tools treat prompts as configuration files rather than as primary creative work. There is real space for a creative-led tools company that treats prompt-writing as the primary discipline and builds the workspace around it.
Creative.competitorLandscape: PromptLayer (promptlayer.com) plays the closest peer in prompt observability. Humanloop (humanloop.com) holds the prompt-engineering platform peer slot. LangSmith (smith.langchain.com) sits in the LLM development middle. Galileo (galileo.ai) plays the LLM evaluation peer reference. We belong alongside Humanloop with a stronger workspace-craft focus.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Prompt Office is an AI tools company building workspaces, evaluation tooling, and version control for prompt-engineering teams.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on treating prompt engineering as a serious discipline. The workspace, the evaluation tools, and the published educational resources all argue for prompt-writing as a primary creative practice.

targetAudience.primary: Prompt engineers, ML engineers, and product engineers responsible for prompts in production systems.
behaviors: Write prompts as a daily practice.
Maintain prompt libraries and version histories.
Run prompt-evaluation regression suites.
Subscribe to LLM-engineering newsletters.
motivations: Want tools that treat prompt-writing as serious work.
Want a workspace built for collaborative prompt iteration.
Want version control and audit trails for prompts in production.

dos: Publish the quarterly essay on prompt-engineering craft.
Reference specific prompt patterns by name.
Show actual prompt examples in marketing.
Sign release notes by the engineer who shipped the feature.

Creative.tagline: We made the model lie. On purpose.
Creative.brandNameRationale: AI's most-feared failure mode becomes the studio's deliberate craft. The name owns the criticism and turns it into a positioning move for creative work.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative AI tools serve writers, designers, and filmmakers using models as collaborators. The market is split between productivity overlays and weird-on-purpose art tools. We're firmly in the second camp.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Runway (runway.ml) holds the creative AI video position. Pika (pika.art) is the playful peer. Krea (krea.ai) sets the real-time creative bar. We sit closer to Krea in tone, closer to Runway in craft.
Creative.positioningStatement: AI tools for creative people who want the model to surprise them.
